_meta.note: Inputs that must all yield 'no data' rather than an empty success or a crash. `raw` is the exact string handed to the parser, so malformed input can be represented too. Each case asserts the same outcome: the parse returns nothing.

cases.name: not json at all
cases.why: A garbage body — e.g. an HTML error page from a proxy — must be caught, not thrown.

cases.name: empty object
cases.why: Valid JSON with nothing recognisable. No windows, no caps, no credits means unusable.

cases.name: only unknown keys
cases.why: Unknown keys are ignored, so this is equivalent to an empty object. Also pins that unknown keys never cause a failure by themselves — the captured payloads carry several.

cases.name: windows present but entirely null
cases.why: Explicit nulls are absence, not zero. This is the shape seen on an account with no active windows and no credits.

cases.name: empty limits array
cases.why: An empty array must not be mistaken for 'windows found'.

cases.name: credits limit explicitly null
cases.why: A null monthly_limit means the account has no credit budget — report no credits rather than a zero budget. Contrast with credits-zero-limit.json, where an actual zero IS reported.

cases.name: truncated json
cases.why: A response cut short mid-stream must fail cleanly rather than half-parse.
